items.reasoning: The handler reads an Open shift, computes expected drawer cash through ShiftReconciliation, reads discrepancy threshold, reconstructs the open Shift aggregate, and returns expected/actual/difference/approval requirement. No write, authorization record, or immutable preview token is created. Read-only preview may become stale after movements, but CloseShiftHandler independently recomputes expected cash and authorization from its close request, so preview staleness alone does not establish a close accounting defect.
items.call_chain: POST /api/shifts/prepare-close -> handler -> ShiftReconciliation.ComputeExpectedCashAsync -> ComputeBreakdownAsync (orders/refunds, drawer expenses, posted cash-in/safe-drop/withdrawals) -> Shift.PrepareBlindClose; close route independently recomputes in CloseShiftHandler.
items.counterevidence: CloseShiftHandler recomputes before final close; existing test asserts expected opening cash plus a cash sale in preview. Existing FIN-004 refund allocation remains separate. No source shows prepare endpoint creates or mutates financial state.
items.test_gaps: Existing test checks ordinary preview total only; no stale-preview/final-recompute behavior test, but static close source is counterevidence. Tests not executed.
items.remaining_action: No new finding from this callable; if UX contract requires preview and close to match, add an integration test that posts a movement between prepare and close and asserts final close uses recomputed total.

items.reasoning: The create route validates basic employee identity fields and parses compensation type case-insensitively, authorizes employees_manage, then copies raw CompensationType and signed DailyWage/ShiftValue/MonthlySalary/OvertimeRate piastres into EmployeeEntity without command-specific sign/range checks. Deterministic emp-{RequestId} replay returns prior row; user link is null. This is an admission path into compensation inputs, not proof that a negative value is actually paid or that caller is unauthorized.
items.call_chain: POST /api/employees -> CreateEmployeeHandler -> EmployeeRules.AssertEmployeeInput + enum parse + employees_manage -> EmployeeEntity -> SaveChanges; later biometric/payroll consumers read stored values.
items.counterevidence: Employee command explicitly requires employees_manage; ordinary cashier UI accepts profile input through this route but no negative-value request behavior was executed. Existing FIN-022 covers enum casing/raw storage. FIN-024 / SEM-MIRROR-057 cover signed earning admission and are the proper linked candidate; no duplicate finding.
items.test_gaps: EmployeeVerticalSliceTests.cs:51-74 covers create/idempotency/permission; 76-89 covers normal update. No negative/zero/upper-bound wage admission case is shown in inspected coverage. Tests not run.
items.remaining_action: Cross-link this additional create-path evidence to existing FIN-024; validate negative/zero employee compensation at the authorized HTTP boundary in future tests, with explicit zero policy. No new finding.

items.reasoning: For a found employee the handler uses Cairo business date and UTC HH:mm, updates or inserts attendance, derives lateness only from a same-business-date open shift, and posts a daily-wage credit only when stored compensation type equals exact Daily. It calls EmployeeLedgerPoster with a deterministic employee/date/shift id, then may post a deterministic late penalty; one SaveChanges persists attendance and pending ledger rows. No explicit wage-positive guard exists on daily wage posting, while late penalty requires positive wage. Event ID is stored but not used as dedup key; deterministic ledger IDs protect same-key movement, and employee/date uniqueness may reject concurrent first attendance.
items.call_chain: POST /api/attendance/check-in -> BiometricCheckInHandler -> SettingsQueryService, attendance row, EmployeeLedgerPoster.PostIfNewAsync for daily wage/penalty -> one SaveChanges; endpoint maps missing employee to 404.
items.counterevidence: Handler comments specify biometric-device authorization model and automatic posting distinct from manual employees_ledger permission; do not infer an auth bypass. Same deterministic id makes repeated same employee/date/shift ledger append a no-op. Existing FIN-022 casing and FIN-024 signed-earning candidate cover the relevant boundaries; no duplicate finding.
items.test_gaps: Existing integration coverage checks a normal daily wage and duplicate event; it does not cover negative stored wages, lower-case type, same Cairo date across UTC midnight, or concurrent first check-in. No tests executed.
items.remaining_action: Cross-reference FIN-024/FIN-022; validate the accepted negative/zero wage behavior and date-boundary/replay semantics in tests under existing device authorization policy.

items.reasoning: The update route validates identity fields/enum, authorizes employees_manage, loads the entity, then replaces compensation type, wage/shift/monthly/overtime values and profile flags with raw request values, with no numeric sign/range validation or optimistic version check. UserId is not changed. Existing evidence supports input admission and last-writer-wins possibility, not an actual concurrent financial loss.
items.call_chain: PUT /api/employees/{employeeId} -> route copies path ID into request -> UpdateEmployeeHandler -> employees_manage -> tracked entity replacement -> SaveChanges; downstream attendance/payroll reads persisted rates.
items.counterevidence: Existing employee management tests prove positive update and preserve UserId. employees_manage gate is explicit. FIN-022 covers raw enum casing and FIN-024/SEM-MIRROR-057 cover signed earning inputs; do not create a second candidate.
items.test_gaps: EmployeeVerticalSliceTests.cs:76-89 only checks a normal positive wage update. Negative/zero bounds and concurrent update against attendance/payroll are not covered by inspected source. Tests not run.
items.remaining_action: Link this source path to FIN-024 and existing FIN-022; future tests should define command-specific negative/zero policy and conflict behavior. No new finding.

items.reasoning: The handler finds employee and today attendance, requires a record, combines stored HH:mm with current UTC date, computes worked/overtime hours, overwrites checkout/hours/event ID, and posts overtime only when hours and stored daily wage are positive. Fixed ledger id is employee/date so repeat checkout with changed derived hours updates attendance but does not revise existing ledger credit. The UTC-date reconstruction can undercount or zero hours when a Cairo business date crosses UTC midnight; this source behavior matches existing FIN-023 candidate. No realized underpayment is established.
items.call_chain: POST /api/attendance/check-out -> BiometricCheckOutHandler -> employee/date attendance + settings + open shift ID -> PayrollRules.CalculateOvertimeAmount -> EmployeeLedgerPoster fixed id -> SaveChanges; API maps domain exception.
items.counterevidence: Existing FIN-023 already tracks date-reconstruction path; handler rejects checkout without attendance and gates auto overtime to positive wage/hours. Current tests only assert no-checkin rejection and zero overtime for a short shift, so do not counterprove UTC boundary behavior. Same deterministic key prevents duplicate row but does not recompute prior amount.
items.test_gaps: No checkout test spanning UTC midnight within one Cairo business date, no positive overtime settlement test, no repeated checkout with changed hour and ledger assertion. Tests not run.
items.remaining_action: Cross-reference FIN-023 without duplicating. Add boundary and repeated-checkout tests to establish intended recalculation/idempotency policy.

items.reasoning: The service builds one selected business-date UTC range, looks up first BusinessDay with that date, then sequentially composes sales, tax, sold product/hourly, expense summary/details, shift summaries, period treasury movements plus current balances, employee rows, inventory, delivery, refunds, audit, printing and backup status. It performs no writes and no shared snapshot transaction; sections can observe different database instants. The selected-day flows versus current balances/status mix is explicit by DTO/queries and should not be called historical balance reconstruction. Duplicate-date FirstOrDefault ambiguity remains conditional on whether multiple BusinessDay rows per date are allowed.
items.call_chain: GET /api/reports/daily-statement -> RequireReportsAccessAsync -> GetAsync(businessDate or BusinessClock.Today) -> report query services and local section builders -> DailyStatementDto.
items.counterevidence: Endpoint requires reports_view. Selected-day query fanout is explicit and current account balances/status are purposefully current. Tests verify normal products and expense detail; no material accounting defect follows solely from lack of a snapshot because no snapshot contract is established. No repeated-date policy or schema constraint was checked.
items.test_gaps: DailyStatementVerticalSliceTests.cs:75-81 permission and 85-116 ordinary sales/expense section behavior. No cross-section consistent-snapshot test under concurrent writes; no duplicate BusinessDay date test. Tests not run.
items.remaining_action: No new finding. If a point-in-time statement is required, define snapshot consistency and test concurrent mutation; if date uniqueness is invariant, prove it at schema/domain boundary or test the selection rule.
